_about: Declarative ERC violation taxonomy + Intent Confidence Layer. This is the SINGLE source of truth that routes every kicad-cli ERC violation into one of four tiers before any fix is attempted: safe_auto (deterministic Python may apply it), needs_reasoning (never auto-fixed; surface root cause + candidate fixes to the LLM/human), forbidden (a dangerous class the AI must NEVER touch even if a candidate exists), or ignore (handled elsewhere / benign — emit nothing). Keys are the EXACT KiCad ERC settings-key strings emitted by `kicad-cli sch erc` (from eeschema/erc/erc_item.cpp), NOT custom names. tools/erc_autofix.py reads this; no classification literals live in Python.
_enabled_note: When false (or this file missing/unparseable), erc_autofix falls straight through to the legacy per-type dispatch — behaviour is byte-stable. When true, the taxonomy router runs FIRST. Three executor kinds: executor="legacy" passes through the original per-type strategies (unconnected_wire_endpoint, duplicate_reference, power_pin_not_driven) unchanged; executor="verb" (2026-06-09: pin_not_connected, endpoint_off_grid, wire_dangling) builds concrete apply_ops from requires_verb + the ERC coords and APPLIES them (confidence-gated + regression-guarded) — gated globally by layout_config.json:erc_autofix.verb_executors; executor="diagnostic" (or anything else) emits a structured root-cause + candidate-fix note without touching the schematic. Flip a single type back to "diagnostic" to stop auto-applying just that one.
_default_note: Any KiCad ERC settings-key not listed in `classes` and not in `ignore_types` is treated as needs_reasoning — i.e. NEVER auto-fixed. Safe by construction: an unknown violation can only ever be escalated, never auto-applied.
_ignore_note: Types the engine already handles correctly (rail labelling, annotation), library/style hygiene nits, or things outside the schematic-repair scope. isolated_pin_label stays here to preserve the current silent-skip behaviour (the engine labels rails correctly). Move a type out of this list into `classes` to start surfacing it.

unconnected_wire_endpoint._note: Existing strategy in erc_autofix._propose_fixes. executor=legacy => router passes through unchanged (byte-stable).

power_pin_not_driven._note: Existing strategy already runs its OWN trace_net-based confidence (already_driven => do nothing; missing_wire => draw wire; no_driver => PWR_FLAG). executor=legacy => byte-stable pass-through; do NOT double-gate with the generic confidence layer.

wire_dangling._phase: ACTIVE (2026-06-09): executor=verb routes this through the existing apply_ops delete_wire verb (tight delete_wire_tol_mm). Regression-guarded. Set executor back to 'diagnostic' to disable.
candidate_fixes: Delete the dangling wire segment, OR extend it so its free end lands on a real pin/junction.

endpoint_off_grid.user_name: Pin or wire end off the connection grid
endpoint_off_grid._phase: ACTIVE (2026-06-09): executor=verb routes this through the apply_ops snap_endpoint verb (wire-ends only; a symbol pin off grid returns no-op and stays for manual review). Confidence-gated + regression-guarded. Set executor back to 'diagnostic' to disable.
candidate_fixes: Snap the off-grid endpoint to the nearest 1.27 mm grid point so the wire/pin actually connects.

pin_not_connected._phase: ACTIVE (2026-06-09): executor=verb routes this through the apply_ops add_no_connect verb. Intent confidence: a genuinely-unused pin (no nearby wire/label) => HIGH => No-Connect flag applied; a pin with a wire/label a grid away => LOW => demoted to needs_reasoning (probable missing wire-snap, never auto-capped). Regression-guarded. Set executor back to 'diagnostic' to disable.
candidate_fixes: HIGH confidence (no nearby net): add a No-Connect (X) flag — the pin is intentionally unused.
LOW confidence (wire/label one grid away): likely a missing wire-snap — extend the wire onto the pin instead of flagging it.

pin_not_driven.user_name: Input pin not driven by any output pins
candidate_fixes: Add a driver (output / bidirectional / tri-state) onto this net.
If the input is meant to be tied to a level, add a pull-up or pull-down to the correct rail (design-dependent — do NOT guess the rail).
If the pin is genuinely unused, add a No-Connect flag.

different_unit_net.user_name: Shared multi-unit pin assigned to different nets
candidate_fixes: A unit-0 (shared) pin of a multi-unit symbol is on two different nets. Decide the single correct net and remove the other connection.
Check the IR: the shared power/IO pin must appear in exactly one net's pin list.

multiple_net_names.user_name: More than one name given to this net/bus
candidate_fixes: Two distinct labels collide on one physical net. Pick ONE canonical name (usually the power-rail name like +3V3/GND, or the most descriptive signal) and rename the others.
Verify the two labels are actually meant to be the same net before merging — they may indicate an accidental short.
The symbol has duplicate pin numbers wired to different nets — a library symbol defect or a wrong net assignment. Fix the symbol pinout or the net membership.

ground_pin_not_ground.user_name: Ground pin not connected to a ground net
candidate_fixes: A pin typed as ground is on a non-ground net. Route it to GND, OR correct the pin's electrical type in the library if mislabelled.
A multi-unit IC has a power-input pin (VCC/AVCC/VDDIO) that the IR never placed. Add the missing pin to the appropriate power net.
A sheet pin has no matching hierarchical label inside the child sheet (or vice-versa). Align the names, or add the missing label/pin.

pin_to_pin_subclassifier._about: KiCad emits a SINGLE settings-key `pin_to_pin` for every pin-conflict-matrix violation; the actual conflict (output-output, power-output short, etc.) lives ONLY in the human-readable description text (KiCad format is typically 'Pins of type <A> and <B> are connected'). This second stage reads (message + all location descrs), lowercased, and routes to a forbidden sub-class or to generic needs_reasoning. SAFETY: pin_to_pin is NEVER safe_auto, so a mis-route between forbidden and needs_reasoning is harmless — both refuse to auto-fix. Matching is purely additive labelling for the human/LLM. First matching rule wins. Token/phrase lists are lowercase substrings; tune them once real kicad-cli pin_to_pin descr strings are captured on this project.
default_candidate_fixes: A pin-type conflict was detected but the exact pair could not be sub-classified. Inspect both pins' electrical types and decide the correct topology — do NOT auto-connect.

pwr_flag_autofix._about: SAFE auto-fix that runs BEFORE the forbidden power_output_conflict rule. A `pin_to_pin` Power-output conflict whose conflicting symbols are PWR_FLAG annotations (refs matching ref_prefixes, e.g. #FLG001/#FLG002) is a REDUNDANT duplicate flag, not a real short — a PWR_FLAG carries no current, it only asserts 'this rail is driven'. The strategy deletes the extra flag(s): if a real driver also shares the net every flag is removed, otherwise the first flag is kept and the rest deleted. Always re-validated by the regression guard, so a flag that was actually masking an undriven rail gets restored. Set enabled=false to revert to treating ALL power-output conflicts as forbidden.
candidate_fixes: Delete the redundant PWR_FLAG(s); a single driver (real power_out or one flag) per rail is enough.

rules.name: power_output_conflict
candidate_fixes: Two power outputs are shorted on one net. REMOVE one driver, or isolate them (ORing diodes / load-switch). The AI must NOT auto-wire or pick a winner.

rules.name: vcc_gnd_short
candidate_fixes: A power pin and a ground pin appear connected — a hard short. STOP. Human review required; never auto-fix.

rules.name: output_output_conflict
candidate_fixes: Two logic outputs drive one net. Insert a buffer/mux, add series isolation, or remove one source. The AI must NOT auto-connect.

rules.name: analog_signal_conflict
rules._weak: KiCad rarely flags passive-passive as a conflict; this rule is mostly documentation of intent. Harmless if it never matches (default is needs_reasoning, also no-auto-fix).
candidate_fixes: A passive/analog conflict was reported. Verify the intended topology by hand — the AI must NOT auto-fix analog connections.

confidence._about: Intent Confidence Layer. Even a safe_auto violation is only auto-applied when its confidence score >= the type's confidence_threshold. Below the threshold the fix is demoted to a needs_reasoning diagnostic with the scoring factors surfaced, so a genuinely-unused pin gets a No-Connect flag while a pin with a wire one grid away is flagged as a probable missing snap instead of being blindly capped.
confidence._near_note: A wire endpoint or label within near_mm of a violation coord, but not ON the pin, signals a likely missing wire-snap — confidence drops to near_obstruction_score.

endpoint_off_grid._note: Off-grid endpoints are mechanically safe to snap; high default. Real scoring (distance to nearest grid + whether a pin sits there) lands with the Phase 3 snap_endpoint verb.
